spec.goal: Add an optional `limit` query parameter to the existing `GET /items` collection route in toy/src/app.js so clients paging a large list can cap the response size. When `limit` is absent the route behaves exactly as it does today (200 with every item as a JSON array in insertion order). When `limit` is present it must be a canonical positive decimal integer — one or more ASCII digits, no leading zero, no sign, no decimal point, no exponent, no surrounding whitespace, and within JavaScript's safe-integer range (matching `/^[1-9][0-9]*$/` and `Number.isSafeInteger`), which is the same canonical-decimal-integer convention already used by `GET /items/:id`. A valid limit returns the first N items in insertion order (ascending id), or all items when N is greater than or equal to the number stored. Any other value — zero, negative, non-numeric, non-canonical, out of safe range, empty, or repeated (`?limit=1&limit=2`, which Express parses to an array) — returns 400 with the JSON body exactly `{ "error": "invalid limit" }` and changes nothing. Validation is scoped to the `GET /items` collection route only; `limit` on any other route is ignored, and unknown query parameters on `GET /items` are ignored. No other route, response shape, or storage behavior changes.

Adding a DELETE /items/:id route or admin-token auth (wi-4 is not present in toy/src/app.js and must not be introduced here).

Any file outside toy/ — no workflow, agent, substrate, or contract changes.

No breaking changes to existing route contracts (GET /items/:id, POST /items, GET /health unchanged)
No changes to stored data shape, storage layer, or in-memory Map

spec.goal: Replace Express's default HTML 404 with a JSON 404 for every request that matches no route in the toy app. Any method/path combination that falls through all registered routes must respond 404 with Content-Type application/json and body exactly {"error":"not found"}, matching the shape GET /items/:id already returns. All existing routes (GET /health, GET /items, POST /items, GET /items/:id) and their status codes, bodies and error payloads are unchanged, and the change must not convert real errors (e.g. malformed JSON bodies rejected by express.json()) into 404s. Implemented as a terminal catch-all handler registered in toy/src/app.js after every route, so it applies to each app instance returned by createApp().

tasks.description: Add a terminal catch-all 404 handler in toy/src/app.js that responds with JSON {"error":"not found"} for any request matching no route. The handler must set Content-Type to application/json, preserve all existing route behavior, not intercept real errors from express.json() or route handlers, apply per app instance, and pass all acceptance tests including the full npm test suite.

spec.goal: Add an optional `sort` query parameter to `GET /items` in toy/src/app.js. `?sort=name` returns items ordered by `name` ascending using a plain code-unit string comparison (no locale/collation, no case folding); `?sort=id` and an absent `sort` both return the existing insertion order. Any other present value — including an empty string, a differently-cased or padded variant, or a repeated parameter — returns 400 with the exact body { "error": "invalid sort" } and no items. The handler must be structured as a filter -> sort -> cap pipeline so that when wi-6 (?q) and wi-5 (?limit) land, filtering happens first, then sorting, then the cap. No other route, and no stored Item shape, changes.

acceptance.then: 200 with content-type application/json; charset=utf-8 and the body is the three items in the order apple, banana, cherry — each object deep-equal to the item returned by its POST

acceptance.then: 200 and the three items appear in id order 1, 2, 3 — equal names keep insertion order (stable sort)

No critical surface touched: not auth, secrets, payments, or infrastructure; isolated to GET /items query handling
Fully reversible: self-contained feature with no persistent state impact
Low environmental risk: no external consumers, self-funded toy venture, additive API changes routine per project context

tasks.description: Implement the `sort` query parameter handler in the GET /items endpoint. Add validation logic that accepts exactly "name" or "id" (case-sensitive, no trimming, no arrays); return 400 with { "error": "invalid sort" } for any other value including empty strings and repeated parameters. When sort=name, apply plain code-unit string comparison (no locale/collation). When sort=id or absent, preserve insertion order. Structure the handler as a filter → sort → cap pipeline to support future query parameters (?q for filtering, ?limit for capping). Ensure the implementation does not mutate the stored insertion order and that all existing tests continue to pass.

spec.goal: Add an optional `q` query parameter to `GET /items` in `toy/src/app.js` that filters the returned list to items whose `name` contains `q` as a case-insensitive substring, preserving insertion order. A missing or empty `q` returns everything, exactly as today. Non-matching searches return `200 []`, never 404. Two decisions the work item leaves open are fixed here so implementer, test author and lenses read the same contract: (a) matching is plain, literal `String.prototype.includes` on both sides lower-cased with `toLowerCase()` — no trimming, no regex, no accent folding, no Unicode normalization; (b) a `q` that Express does not parse as a string (repeated `?q=a&q=b`, or bracketed `?q[x]=y`) is rejected with `400 { "error": "invalid q" }`, matching the project's existing `invalid limit` / `invalid sort` error convention rather than silently guessing which value the client meant. DEPENDENCY: `GET /items` on the current base does NOT yet support `?limit=N` (that is wi-5, still unimplemented — the handler today is `res.json([...items.values()])`). This spec does not add `limit`. AC-11 through AC-13 specify the filter-then-cap ordering and are testable only on a base where wi-5 has already landed; if this task is implemented before or beside wi-5, the implementer must still structure the handler so the `q` filter is applied to the full insertion-ordered list before any later capping step, and the combination tests are held until wi-5 merges.

spec.goal: Every Item stored by the toy API carries a third field, created_at: a server-generated ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (Z-suffixed, millisecond precision, e.g. "2026-09-10T17:00:00.000Z") recorded at the moment the item is created. The Item shape becomes exactly { id, name, created_at }, and that full shape is returned by POST /items (201), GET /items, and GET /items/:id (200). The timestamp is assigned once, by the server, from the system clock at creation time; it is never re-derived on read, never mutated, and never taken from client input. All other behavior is unchanged: id assignment and its non-consumption on rejected requests, name validation (400 "name is required" for missing/empty/non-string, 400 "name too long" above 64 UTF-16 code units), 404 "not found" semantics including non-canonical integer ids, JSON content types, and the GET /health body. The existing suite in toy/test/items.test.js compares Items API-response-to-API-response (e.g. assert.deepEqual(list, [item])), so those assertions remain valid rather than breaking; they must be extended — not weakened or deleted — so the new field is actually asserted instead of silently carried along, and any assertion enumerating an Item's keys must now expect created_at.
